text:
**Mistral just released a ~1-trillion-parameter open-weight model, and it's strong at cybersecurity.**

Mistral Large 4, nicknamed "Le Chonk," is now on Hugging Face. A few things stood out to me:

🔐 **It does security work that some closed models refuse.**
On the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index, the model has to reproduce a real vulnerability in open-source software and then patch it. ML4 scored 82%, the highest reported result on that test. Mistral says several closed frontier models score near zero because they decline the task.

This matters for defenders. You usually can't fix a vulnerability without first reproducing it. Incident response and vuln research also look a lot like attacks to a content filter. With open weights, the deployment and usage policy are under your control, so a provider can't cut off access in the middle of an incident.

It still refuses harmful requests. On cyber prompts from JailbreakBench, StrongREJECT, and AgentHarm, its average refusal rate is higher than any other open-weight model.

🧠 **Two kinds of sparsity in one model**
• Mixture-of-Experts: about 1T total parameters, with 4 of 128 experts plus 1 shared expert active per token
• DeepSeek-style sparse attention: each query attends to at most 2,048 key positions
• 1M-token context window
• A 1.6B Pixtral vision encoder for image input

📊 **Benchmark results**
• 93% on Cybench (40 security-competition challenges)
• 61.7% on DeepSWE v1.1
• 49.8% on the Coding Agent Index, ahead of DeepSeek V4 Pro and Qwen3.8 Max
• 93.3% prompt-injection resistance on Lakera's B3
• #5 open-weight model on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index

⚙️ **Support from day one**
Transformers, vLLM (including an NVFP4 checkpoint for Blackwell), llama.cpp GGUFs, TRL fine-tuning, Inference Endpoints, and Dell Enterprise Hub all work at launch. The 2-bit quant runs on a single 512GB M3 Ultra at about 15 tokens/second.

💡 **What I find most interesting:** reproduce-then-patch tasks have a verifiable reward. That makes them a good fit for RL environments. Teams could distill ML4's patching traces into smaller security models trained on their own codebases, crash logs, and malware samples.

The license is the Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License. It's derived from MIT but restricts model-as-a-service offerings, so read it before you build a product on top.

Strong security capability in an open model could be a big win for defenders, and I'm curious what the community builds with it.

What would you build with this? 👇

#AI #OpenSource #Cybersecurity #LLM #MachineLearning #HuggingFace #Mistral

*Note:* The article says the model has 49B active parameters, but the model ID is `Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B`. I left the active-parameter count out of the post. Check the model card before you add it.
